annotation.title_clean: Artificial Intelligence: Interrogating the Prospect of a Robot Lawyer to Practice Law in Nigeria
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence: Interrogating the Prospect of a Robot Lawyer to Practice Law in Nigeria
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ikubanni, O.; Oyebanji, O.; Aidonojie, P.A.; Oyebade, A.A.; Aderibigbe, O.; Huraira, M.
annotation.summary_en: Doctrinal Nigerian law journal article assessing whether AI 'robot lawyers' like DoNotPay can practice law in Nigeria. Finds Nigerian legal practice statutes do not recognise robots as licensed persons, and recommends amending the Legal Practitioners Act and Legal Education Act and conferring personhood status, while noting ethical concerns.
key_provisions_or_claims: Nigerian law does not recognise robot lawyers as persons licensed to practice law.
Robot lawyers need personhood status before they can practice in Nigeria.
Recommends amending the Legal Practitioners Act and Legal Education (Consolidation) Act.
AI and robot lawyers are inevitable and can enhance access and efficiency in legal practice.
Cautions that licensing robots for practice raises ethical concerns and may endanger humans.
